description: With the divine eye Arjuna sees the whole world, divided in many ways, standing as one in the body of the god of gods (11.13): many mouths, eyes, arms and bellies, divine ornaments, garlands and weapons, facing every way, without beginning, middle or end, the gods, Brahmā on the lotus, the seers and all hosts of beings within it (11.10–11, 11.15–16); then a fierce form touching the sky, with gaping mouths and blazing eyes, into which the worlds and the warriors of both sides rush (11.20–30).
stage: granted by the Lord's grace through a divine eye (11.8, 11.47)

description: The Lord declares that Arjuna cannot see him with his own eye and gives him a divine eye (divyaṃ cakṣuḥ) to behold his sovereign yoga (11.8).

The light of the form is like the light of a thousand suns risen at once in the sky (11.12); it is a mass of splendour shining on every side, hard to look upon, with the radiance of blazing fire and sun (11.17).

Filled with amazement, his hair standing on end, Arjuna bows his head with joined palms (11.14); after the Lord declares himself Time he trembles, bows, prostrates and speaks stammering, greatly afraid (11.35).

Seeing the fierce form, Arjuna says the three worlds and he himself are shaken; shaken in his inner self he finds neither steadiness (dhṛti) nor calm (śama), does not know the directions and finds no shelter (11.20, 11.23–25); having seen what was never seen before he is thrilled and his mind (manas) is shaken with fear (11.45).

Arjuna sees the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra with the kings, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa and warriors of his own side rushing into the Lord's mouths, some caught between the teeth with heads crushed, entering like rivers into the ocean and like moths into a blazing fire, while the Lord licks up the worlds with flaming mouths (11.26–30).
Told to be without fear and with a glad mind, Arjuna sees again the Lord's own gentle, human form and says he is now composed (sacetāḥ) and has returned to his natural state (prakṛti) (11.49–51).
Those whose thought is on the Lord, awakening one another and always speaking of him, are content and take delight (tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca) (10.9).
